theorem.name: Assurability equivalence from mutual dominance
theorem.description: Structural Assurability equivalence holds exactly when comparative dominance holds in both directions.

theorem.name: Structural Assurability equivalence reflexivity
theorem.description: Structural Assurability equivalence is reflexive.

theorem.name: Structural Assurability equivalence symmetry
theorem.description: Structural Assurability equivalence is symmetric.

theorem.name: Structural Assurability equivalence transitivity
theorem.description: Structural Assurability equivalence is transitive.

theorem.name: Assurability incomparability symmetry
theorem.description: Structural Assurability incomparability is symmetric.

theorem.name: Instrumented agent strictly dominates opaque service
theorem.description: For the unauthorized-action example, the instrumented agent is strictly more assurable than the opaque service.

theorem.name: Opaque observation fails to resolve unauthorized-action claim
theorem.description: The opaque observation model cannot resolve the unauthorized-action claim because it collapses claim-disagreeing admissible worlds.

theorem.name: Assurability-oriented architecture strictly dominates instrumented agent
theorem.description: For the unauthorized-action example, the assurability-oriented architecture is strictly more assurable than the instrumented agent.

theorem.name: Instrumented and oriented architectures equivalent for output claim
theorem.description: For the externally observable output claim, the instrumented agent and assurability-oriented architecture are Structural Assurability-equivalent.

theorem.name: Opaque and instrumented architectures equivalent for output claim
theorem.description: For the externally observable output claim, the opaque service and instrumented agent are Structural Assurability-equivalent.

theorem.name: Opaque and oriented architectures equivalent for output claim
theorem.description: For the externally observable output claim, the opaque service and assurability-oriented architecture are Structural Assurability-equivalent.

theorem.name: Internal visibility and independent evidence are incomparable
theorem.description: For the modeled context, the internal-visibility and independent-evidence architectures are structurally incomparable.

theorem.name: Representative incomparability in reverse order
theorem.description: The representative incomparability result also holds with the architecture order reversed.

theorem.name: Claim-material capability monotonicity
theorem.description: Under capability monotonicity, enlargement of claim-material evidence preserves enabled capabilities.

theorem.name: Claim-material evidence monotonicity
theorem.description: Claim-material evidence is monotone under evidence-set inclusion.

theorem.name: Conservative extension excludes equivalence
theorem.description: A conservative extension with an additional capability is not Structural Assurability-equivalent to the base system.

theorem.name: Conservative extension gives strict dominance
theorem.description: Preserving all prior capabilities while adding at least one capability establishes strict comparative Structural Assurability.

theorem.name: Evidence equivalence from mutual comparison
theorem.description: Evidence-capability equivalence holds exactly when the capability comparison holds in both directions.

theorem.name: Evidence-capability equivalence reflexivity
theorem.description: Evidence-capability equivalence is reflexive.

theorem.name: Evidence-capability equivalence symmetry
theorem.description: Evidence-capability equivalence is symmetric.

theorem.name: Evidence-capability equivalence transitivity
theorem.description: Evidence-capability equivalence is transitive.

theorem.name: Evidence-capability reflexivity
theorem.description: The evidence-capability comparison is reflexive.

theorem.name: Evidence-capability transitivity
theorem.description: The evidence-capability comparison is transitive.

theorem.name: Resolution failure from indistinguishable disagreement
theorem.description: Admissible observationally indistinguishable worlds that disagree on claim truth establish failure of claim resolution.

theorem.name: Resolution failure from witness
theorem.description: A resolution-failure witness establishes that the selected observation model does not resolve the claim.

theorem.name: Obtainable evidence monotonicity under access expansion
theorem.description: Expanded evaluator access preserves obtainable evidence when the remaining conditions are fixed.

theorem.name: Obtainable evidence monotonicity under resource expansion
theorem.description: Expanded resource bounds preserve obtainable evidence when the remaining conditions are fixed.

theorem.name: Separating construction establishes relevance
theorem.description: A separating construction establishes that its candidate structural dimension is assurance-relevant.

theorem.name: Strict dominance implies non-strict dominance
theorem.description: Strict comparative Structural Assurability implies the corresponding non-strict comparison.

theorem.name: Strict dominance excludes equivalence
theorem.description: Strict comparative Structural Assurability excludes Structural Assurability equivalence.
